hypothesis: The daily stable-excess frontier card found no edge from risk/trend state with zero return forecast. The one locally demonstrated signal is the intraday early-session path: an observable opening move that may continue into the same-session remainder. Test, self-contained and with no parent model, whether a bounded causal threshold family on the opening 09:30-to-10:30 return produces stable excess over SOXX buy-and-hold on the same 10:30-to-close window.
parameter_search_budget: one pre-registered bounded threshold family; no tuning after outcomes

signal_definition.observation: session open (09:45 bar open) through 10:30 close
signal_definition.decision: target chosen at 10:30 close using only the observable early return
signal_definition.causality: no overnight position; the open-to-10:30 path is fully observable before the traded window

allocation.long: early return >= long_threshold -> 100% SOXL for the rest of the session
allocation.short: early return <= -short_threshold -> 100% cash for the rest of the session
allocation.neutral: otherwise 100% SOXX for the rest of the session
allocation.fees: turnover from the prior 10:30 target charged at cost_bps

selection: development-only deterministic ranking by stable-excess satisfaction, then positive years, Sharpe difference and drawdown improvement; the off/benchmark control is never selectable

gates.stable_excess: beats SOXX return AND drawdown AND Sharpe on the window, with at least minimum_positive_years annual wins
gates.promotion: development AND reused_diagnostic stable excess at both 10bps and 25bps

stopping: Exactly the pre-registered family at two costs across three windows; no threshold, window or cost tuning after outcomes. Preserve all results, including failures.
limitations: The 10:30 decision price is assumed fillable; bid/ask, queue and latency are not modeled.
Only the 10:30-to-close window is traded; overnight and morning exposure are deliberately absent.
The forward window is only the newly available sessions and is statistically weak.
A negative result does not refute lower-turnover, state-conditioned intraday mechanisms.
